## Summary
Implement the HetioNet 2-hop neighborhood import step that takes a resolved CUI, queries the seeded HetioNet subgraph in Neo4j for related nodes within 2 hops, and creates relationship edges between the SubConcept and relevant biomedical entities (genes, diseases, compounds, anatomy, side effects) capped at 10 nodes per type.

## User story
As a curriculum architect, I want SubConcepts enriched with mechanistic biomedical relationships from HetioNet, so that generated assessment items can test clinical reasoning about drug-gene-disease pathways.

## Why this matters
HetioNet relationships enable the generation of "mechanism of action" and "drug interaction" style questions — high-value USMLE Step 1 content. Without this enrichment, assessment items are limited to surface-level recall. Importing too many nodes (no cap) would explode the graph and degrade query performance; importing too few would miss critical relationships.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a resolved CUI, query HetioNet subgraph in Neo4j for nodes within 2 hops
- [ ] BFS traversal limited to exactly 2 hops (no deeper)
- [ ] Maximum 10 nodes imported per node type (Gene, Disease, Compound, Anatomy, SideEffect)
- [ ] Imported nodes linked to SubConcept via typed edges (ASSOCIATED_WITH, TARGETS, TREATS, etc.)
- [ ] All imported relationships carry `source: 'hetionet'` provenance
- [ ] Supabase enrichment log updated FIRST, Neo4j edges SECOND (Rule 6)
- [ ] All Neo4j writes via neo4jQuery (Rule 1)
- [ ] Step returns import summary: `{ nodes_imported: number, edges_created: number, types: Record<string, number> }`
- [ ] If CUI not found in HetioNet, step returns empty result gracefully (not failure)

## Canonical decisions in play

| Rule 6 (G08) | Write import log to Supabase FIRST, then create Neo4j edges |

## Code patterns to follow
```typescript
// Pattern: BFS 2-hop with per-type cap
import { neo4jQuery } from '@journey/neo4j/client';
import { createServerClient } from '@journey/db/server';

const MAX_NODES_PER_TYPE = 10;
const MAX_HOPS = 2;

export async function importHetionetNeighborhood(
  subconcept_id: string,
  institution_id: string,
  cui: string
) {
  const supabase = createServerClient();

  // 1. BFS 2-hop query from HetioNet seed node matching CUI
  const neighbors = await neo4jQuery(
    `MATCH (source:HetioNet_Node {identifier: $cui, institution_id: $inst})
     CALL apoc.path.subgraphNodes(source, {
       maxLevel: $maxHops,
       relationshipFilter: '>',
       limit: 100
     }) YIELD node
     WITH node, labels(node)[0] AS nodeType
     WITH nodeType, collect(node)[0..$maxPerType] AS capped
     UNWIND capped AS n
     RETURN n.identifier AS id, n.name AS name, nodeType`,
    { cui, inst: institution_id, maxHops: MAX_HOPS, maxPerType: MAX_NODES_PER_TYPE }
  );

  // 2. Supabase FIRST (Rule 6)
  await supabase.from('subconcept_enrichment_log').insert({
    subconcept_id,
    step: 'hetionet-import',
    result: { nodes_imported: neighbors.records.length },
  });

  // 3. Neo4j edges SECOND (Rule 1)
  // Create ASSOCIATED_WITH edges in batch
  await neo4jQuery(
    `UNWIND $nodes AS n
     MATCH (sc:SubConcept {uuid: $subconcept_id, institution_id: $inst})
     MATCH (target {identifier: n.id, institution_id: $inst})
     MERGE (sc)-[:ASSOCIATED_WITH {source: 'hetionet', hop_distance: n.hop}]->(target)`,
    { subconcept_id, inst: institution_id, nodes: neighbors.records }
  );
}
```

## Code patterns to AVOID
```typescript
// ✗ AP-01: Raw neo4j-driver import
import { driver } from 'neo4j-driver'; // BANNED

// ✗ No cap on imported nodes — causes graph explosion

// ✗ Rule 6: Neo4j before Supabase
await neo4jQuery(...); // WRONG ORDER

// ✗ Promise.all for batch imports
await Promise.all(types.map(importType)); // BANNED — use Promise.allSettled
```

## Rollback procedure
If implementation fails mid-way:
1. No SQL migrations to reverse
2. Neo4j: `MATCH ()-[r:ASSOCIATED_WITH {source: 'hetionet'}]->() DELETE r`
3. git stash && git checkout develop
